identification.summary: Mandiant's TEMP.Hermit is a North Korean cyber activity cluster active since at least 2013, targeting government, defense, telecommunications and financial institutions worldwide in what Mandiant describes as Pyongyang's efforts to collect strategic intelligence [S1]. Mandiant says it is the cluster most frequently aligned with public 'Lazarus Group' reporting [S1]. Mandiant suspects with high confidence that its UNC2970 cluster is UNC577, also known as TEMP.Hermit [S2]. UNC4034 was merged into UNC2970 based on infrastructure, tooling and TTP overlaps [S2].
identification.firstObserved: Mandiant: active since at least 2013 [S1][S2]. UNC2970 specifically: Mandiant detected a phishing campaign against a US technology company in June 2022 [S2] and later described UNC2970 as active since 2021 [S3].
identification.notes: Vendor cluster boundaries differ. Microsoft's Diamond Sleet (formerly ZINC) is described by Microsoft as overlapping with TEMP.Hermit and Labyrinth Chollima, not identical to it [S4]. Mandiant tracks TEMP.Hermit, APT38 and Andariel separately and calls 'Lazarus Group' an umbrella term in open-source reporting [S1]. The February 2018 FireEye Adobe Flash zero-day reporting listed in the imported record concerns TEMP.Reaper (Cisco: Group 123), a different FireEye cluster, and is not evidence for TEMP.Hermit [S6].

attribution.sponsor: North Korea. Mandiant assesses TEMP.Hermit, APT38 and Andariel are likely subordinate to Lab 110 within the Reconnaissance General Bureau (RGB) 3rd Bureau (Foreign Intelligence) [S1]. Mandiant describes UNC2970 as a cyber espionage group suspected to have a North Korea nexus [S3].
attribution.confidence: Mandiant: UNC2970 is UNC577/TEMP.Hermit with high confidence (suspected) [S2]. The RGB subordination is stated by Mandiant as 'likely' [S1]. No government attribution was found in the sources gathered.
attribution.basis: Mandiant cites malware code overlaps, infrastructure and TTPs for the UNC2970 to UNC577 link [S2]. The Lab 110 assessment is Mandiant's analysis of RGB organization, with shared infrastructure, malware and TTPs across DPRK clusters [S1].

objectives: Strategic intelligence collection for Pyongyang [S1]. In the UNC2970 operations, espionage against Western media and technology organizations and security researchers [S2], and later against senior staff in energy and aerospace [S3].

regions: South Korea (primary observed target of UNC577 per Mandiant) [S2]
United States and Europe (media and technology victims, 2022-2023) [S2]
US, UK, Netherlands, Cyprus, Sweden, Germany, Singapore, Hong Kong, Australia (2024 lures) [S3]
targeting.notes: 2024 lures targeted senior and manager-level employees [S3]. In February 2026 GTIG reported UNC2970 used Gemini to profile cybersecurity and defense firms and map technical job roles and salary data, as relayed by press coverage [S5]. Sector list mixes Mandiant's TEMP.Hermit description [S1] and UNC2970 victimology [S2][S3].

capabilities.summary: Social-engineering-led intrusion: fake LinkedIn recruiter personas that move targets to WhatsApp or email, then deliver macro Word documents using remote-template injection, ISO or ZIP archives with trojanized legitimate tools [S2][S3]. 2023 toolset reported by Mandiant includes LIDSHIFT (trojanized TightVNC), LIDSHOT, PLANKWALK, TOUCHSHIFT, TOUCHSHOT, TOUCHKEY, HOOKSHOT, TOUCHMOVE, SIDESHOW (49+ commands) and CLOUDBURST, which was delivered through abuse of a compromised account in Microsoft Intune [S2]. C2 was largely hosted on compromised WordPress sites [S2]. In 2024 the actor used a trojanized SumatraPDF with the BURNBOOK launcher and MISTPEN backdoor, with later variants using Microsoft Graph and OAuth endpoints for C2 [S3]. Mandiant notes TEMP.Hermit shares code and complete tools with other DPRK operators [S2]. Microsoft attributes a 2023 CyberLink installer supply-chain compromise (LambLoad) to Diamond Sleet, a cluster that overlaps with TEMP.Hermit [S4].

campaigns.name: Mandiant 'Not So Lazarus' DPRK organization assessment
campaigns.summary: Mandiant publishes TEMP.Hermit as a distinct RGB cluster active since at least 2013, likely subordinate to Lab 110, separate from APT38 and Andariel [S1].

campaigns.name: UNC2970 phishing of US technology company
campaigns.summary: Mandiant detects a phishing campaign against a US technology company and suspects security researchers were targeted; later responses involved US and European media organizations hit by job-recruitment spear-phishing [S2].

campaigns.name: UNC2970 LinkedIn/WhatsApp recruiter campaign (LIGHTSHOW report)
campaigns.summary: Fake recruiter accounts on LinkedIn, WhatsApp delivery, macro documents and a trojanized TightVNC 'skills test'; new families such as TOUCHMOVE and SIDESHOW; CLOUDBURST pushed via Intune; overlaps with Operation Dream Job reporting [S2].

campaigns.name: CyberLink supply-chain compromise (Microsoft, Diamond Sleet)
campaigns.summary: Microsoft attributes a modified, validly signed CyberLink installer (LambLoad) affecting over 100 devices in Japan, Taiwan, Canada and the US to Diamond Sleet, which Microsoft says overlaps with TEMP.Hermit. Mandiant did not tie this to UNC2970 in the sources gathered [S4].

campaigns.name: UNC2970 trojanized PDF reader campaign
campaigns.summary: Mandiant first identified the activity in June 2024 and reported it 17 September 2024: password-protected ZIP with encrypted PDF and modified SumatraPDF, BURNBOOK launcher, MISTPEN backdoor, aimed at energy and aerospace senior staff and US critical infrastructure workers [S3].

campaigns.name: GTIG reports UNC2970 use of Gemini for reconnaissance
campaigns.summary: Press coverage of a Google Threat Intelligence Group report says UNC2970 used Gemini to synthesize OSINT and profile high-value targets, including cybersecurity and defense firms and technical job roles [S5].

diamond.adversary: North Korean RGB-linked operators, likely within the Lab 110 grouping, tracked by Mandiant as TEMP.Hermit/UNC577 and UNC2970 [S1][S2].
diamond.capability: Recruiter-themed social engineering, trojanized legitimate software (TightVNC, SumatraPDF, Notepad++ plugins), DLL sideloading, in-memory loaders and cloud-service abuse including Intune [S2][S3].
diamond.infrastructure: Compromised WordPress sites for C2, a compromised university SharePoint domain, and Microsoft Graph/OAuth endpoints in later MISTPEN variants; LinkedIn and WhatsApp for victim contact [S2][S3].
diamond.victim: Government, defense, telecommunications, finance, media, technology, security researchers, energy and aerospace staff [S1][S2][S3].
diamond.socioPolitical: Strategic intelligence collection for Pyongyang within the RGB cyber structure [S1].
diamond.technology: Exposure of individuals' professional social-media and messaging channels, user-run archives and unsigned viewer tools, and cloud management consoles (Intune) with weak privileged-account controls [S2][S3].

gaps: UNC2970 to TEMP.Hermit is a suspected (high confidence) mapping by Mandiant; the UNC2970 reports are not the same as all TEMP.Hermit activity [S2].
Microsoft's Diamond Sleet overlaps with TEMP.Hermit but is not identical; Diamond Sleet campaigns such as the CyberLink supply-chain compromise should not be assumed to be UNC2970 [S4].
The 2018 FireEye Adobe Flash zero-day reference in the imported record concerns TEMP.Reaper (Group 123) and was not used as TEMP.Hermit evidence [S6].
No government attribution (DOJ, CISA, Treasury) specific to TEMP.Hermit found in the searches run.
Primary GTIG February 2026 report was not opened; Gemini-use details rely on press coverage [S5].
Mandiant's original 2022 TEMP.Hermit work before 'Not So Lazarus' and victim counts are not public in the sources gathered.
Sources differ on UNC2970's start (2021 per Mandiant 2024 [S3]; tracked from June 2022 per 2023 report [S2]).
No MITRE ATT&CK group ID was identified for TEMP.Hermit in this research pass.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is the individual: senior and manager-level staff in defense, aerospace, energy and technology, their LinkedIn and WhatsApp accounts, and cloud management planes such as Intune [S2][S3]. STEP 2: The adversary exploits human contact channels outside enterprise monitoring and abuses legitimate software and cloud services to blend in [S2][S3]. STEP 3: Template is fake recruiter contact, then archive or document with trojanized legitimate tool, then in-memory backdoor with C2 on compromised WordPress sites or Microsoft Graph, then keylogging and screenshots [S2][S3]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued recruiter-themed targeting of defense-industrial and energy personnel for strategic intelligence [S1][S3]. MDCOA is use of a compromised privileged cloud account to push code to many managed endpoints [S2], or AI-assisted target profiling producing more tailored lures [S5]. Candidate indicators: password-protected ZIPs containing a PDF plus bundled viewer executable, scheduled tasks named 'Sumatra Launcher', unusual DLLs next to signed binaries, Intune device-management scripts created and deleted by one account, and non-browser processes calling graph.microsoft.com [S2][S3].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: brief personnel with defense-industrial access on recruiter-themed approaches via LinkedIn and WhatsApp, and track Mandiant, Microsoft and GTIG reporting for Diamond Sleet, UNC2970 and TEMP.Hermit naming overlaps [S2][S3][S4]. (2) Authorities: monitoring of personal-channel contact is limited to what policy and law allow; coordinate with counterintelligence and legal before acting on personal accounts. (3) Mission assurance: harden privileged cloud administration (cloud-only accounts, phishing-resistant MFA, Intune multi-admin approval, as Mandiant recommends) [S2]. (4) Coordination: share indicators with DC3, DIB partners and service CI elements; keep vendor cluster names distinct in reporting [S1][S4].
